title: Making and Firing IgE: Class Switching, Hyper-IgE and Mast-Cell Mediators
summary: Learn the two signals a B cell needs to switch to IgE, what happens when CD40 ligand is missing or IgE is produced in excess, and which mast-cell mediators are stored versus newly made, including why tryptase must be drawn within hours.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 56 Hits 7 (hyper-IgE/Job syndrome), 13 (IgE class switching; X-linked hyper-IgM), 14 (mast-cell subtypes), 15 (cysteinyl leukotrienes, PGD2), Trap 4 (late tryptase) and the Figure 56 mast-cell degranulation image as a schematic. Checked against Galletta 2024, Durandy & Kracker 2012, Nagata & Suzuki 2022, Krystel-Whittemore 2015, Komi 2020, Kanaoka & Boyce 2014, Rittchen & Heinemann 2019, Domingo 2018, Beck 2019 and Ansotegui 2020. Qualifications: Hit 7 gives IgE 2,000–50,000 kU/L; Galletta 2024 reports 2,000–100,000 IU/mL in STAT3-HIES, falling with age (register flag rv-hies-ige-range). Hit 15 says PGD2 comes via COX-2; mast cells express COX-1 and COX-2, and one study of human lung mast cells found PGD2 relied on COX-1 (register flag rv-pgd2-cox-isoform). The lesson says only “cyclooxygenase pathway”. The reviewer’s “up to 1000×” leukotriene potency is taught as “several orders of magnitude lower doses” for inhaled LTC4 and LTD4 (Kanaoka & Boyce), who note LTE4 is a weaker bronchoconstrictor than LTC4 and LTD4, whereas Hit 15 groups all three (register flag rv-cyslt-lte4-potency). Not taught: mucosal mast cells’ IL-5 dependence and C5a unresponsiveness, histamine content per cell, FcεRI numbers, IgE physical constants.

objectives: Name the two signals required for IgE class switching and predict the immunoglobulin pattern in CD40 ligand deficiency.
Recognize the laboratory and clinical picture of STAT3 hyper-IgE (Job) syndrome.
Classify mast-cell mediators as stored or newly synthesized, distinguish mast-cell subtypes by protease, and time tryptase sampling.

scenes.title: Making IgE, firing IgE
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three requests reach the immunology bench — (1) a boy with eczema, repeated “cold” staphylococcal skin abscesses and lung cysts, total IgE 8,000 IU/mL; (2) a boy with Pneumocystis pneumonia whose IgM is normal but IgG, IgA and IgE are almost absent; (3) an adult whose suspected anaphylaxis tryptase was drawn 3 days later and is normal. Question token: “Fault in making IgE, or in firing it?”

cues.text: Three requests reach the immunology bench. A boy with eczema, cold skin abscesses and lung cysts has a total IgE of eight thousand.
Another boy has Pneumocystis pneumonia, a normal IgM, and almost no IgG, IgA or IgE.
And an adult’s tryptase, drawn three days after a suspected anaphylaxis, is normal. Where did each story go wrong: making IgE, or firing it?

props.label: Fault in making IgE, or in firing it?

scenes.title: Making IgE: two signals
scenes.altText: Schematic: a T helper cell touching a B cell. Signal card 1: IL-4 (and IL-13) binds its receptor on the B cell and activates STAT6. Signal card 2: CD40 on the B cell meets CD40 ligand (CD40L) on the activated T helper cell and activates NF-κB. Result card: STAT6 and NF-κB bind side by side and drive ε germline transcription and AID expression, so the B cell switches its heavy-chain constant region to ε and secretes IgE with the same antigen specificity.

cues.text: A B cell starts by making IgM. To switch to IgE it needs two signals at once.
Signal one is a cytokine. Interleukin 4, and also interleukin 13, act through STAT6.
Signal two is contact. CD40 on the B cell meets CD40 ligand on an activated T helper cell, and that switches on NF kappa B.
Together, STAT6 and NF kappa B drive epsilon germline transcription and the enzyme AID. The constant region is swapped, the variable region is kept, and out comes IgE.

props.title: B cell (IgM)
lines: Needs 2 signals to switch to IgE

scenes.title: Firing IgE: the mast cell
scenes.altText: Schematic: allergen bridging two IgE molecules on FcεRI of a mast cell. Card 1, within minutes, stored granule mediators: histamine, tryptase (all mast cells) and chymase (connective-tissue mast cells only). Card 2, made new from arachidonic acid: cysteinyl leukotrienes LTC4 → LTD4 → LTE4 via 5-lipoxygenase and LTC4 synthase (inhaled LTC4 and LTD4 act at far lower doses than histamine; LTE4 is weaker); prostaglandin D2 via cyclooxygenase and hematopoietic PGD synthase. Card 3: cytokines over hours. Subtype strip: mucosal mast cells = tryptase only; connective-tissue mast cells = tryptase + chymase + carboxypeptidase.

cues.text: IgE sits on the mast cell’s high-affinity receptor, FcεRI. Degranulation through this receptor starts when a multivalent allergen cross-links neighbouring IgE molecules.
Then stored granules empty within minutes: histamine and the protease tryptase. Mucosal mast cells carry tryptase only; connective-tissue mast cells also carry chymase and carboxypeptidase.

The cell also makes new lipid mediators. The 5-lipoxygenase pathway gives the cysteinyl leukotrienes, C4, D4 and E4. Inhaled C4 and D4 constrict airways at doses several orders of magnitude lower than histamine; E4 is weaker. The cyclooxygenase pathway gives prostaglandin D2.
Hours later, newly made cytokines keep the inflammation going.

scenes.title: Reading the bench
scenes.altText: Three result cards. CD40L deficiency (X-linked class-switch defect): normal or raised IgM with absent or very low IgG, IgA and IgE; opportunistic infections such as Pneumocystis and Cryptosporidium. STAT3 hyper-IgE syndrome (autosomal dominant, Job syndrome): IgE above 2,000 IU/mL (reported range 2,000–100,000 IU/mL, may fall with age), eosinophilia, eczema, recurrent cold staphylococcal abscesses, pneumatoceles; DOCK8 deficiency is the usual recessive form. Tryptase: rises steeply, peaks about 1–2 h, half-life about 2 h, back toward baseline within about 24 h — a day-3 value is a baseline, not an acute sample. Hook answers listed.

cues.text: Case two is a making fault. Without CD40 ligand the second signal never arrives: IgM is normal or high, but IgG, IgA and IgE are absent or very low. The gene is X-linked, and opportunistic infections such as Pneumocystis are typical.

Case one is the opposite. Hyper IgE means above two thousand IU per millilitre. With eczema, cold staphylococcal abscesses and pneumatoceles, think STAT3 hyper IgE, or Job, syndrome; DOCK8 deficiency is the usual recessive form.
Case three is a timing fault. Tryptase peaks about one to two hours after onset and falls back toward baseline within about a day, so a day-three sample is a baseline, not proof of no anaphylaxis.
The right plan is an acute sample within a few hours, plus a baseline at least twenty-four hours later.

props.title: CD40L deficiency (X-linked)
lines: IgG, IgA, IgE absent or low

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “A normal tryptase 3 days after the event rules out anaphylaxis” (✓ tryptase returns toward baseline within about 24 h, and a rise is not seen in every anaphylaxis); “X-linked hyper-IgM means too much of every antibody” (✓ only IgM is normal or high; IgG, IgA and IgE are low because CD40L is missing); “Histamine is the strongest airway constrictor from mast cells” (✓ inhaled leukotrienes C4 and D4 act at doses several orders of magnitude lower).

cues.text: Trap one: a normal tryptase three days later rules out anaphylaxis. No: by then tryptase is back at baseline, and not every anaphylaxis raises it.
Trap two: hyper IgM means too much of every antibody. No: only IgM is normal or high; IgG, IgA and IgE are low because the CD40 signal is missing.
Trap three: histamine is the strongest airway constrictor. No: inhaled leukotrienes C4 and D4 work at far lower doses.

props.title: ✗ “Normal day-3 tryptase = no anaphylaxis.”
lines: ✓ Back to baseline by ~24 h; draw within hours

props.title: ✗ “Hyper-IgM = too much of every Ig.”
lines: ✓ IgM up; IgG, IgA, IgE down (no CD40L)

props.title: ✗ “Histamine is the strongest bronchoconstrictor.”
lines: ✓ Inhaled LTC4 and LTD4 act at far lower doses

scenes.title: Signal, handshake, trigger
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “To MAKE IgE a B cell needs a SIGNAL (IL-4/IL-13 → STAT6) and a HANDSHAKE (CD40–CD40L). To FIRE IgE a mast cell needs a TRIGGER (allergen cross-linking). The second C in MCTC is for Chymase and Connective tissue.” Tokens: signal = IL-4/IL-13 · handshake = CD40L · trigger = cross-link. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: to make IgE, a B cell needs a signal, interleukin 4 or 13, and a handshake, CD40 with its ligand. To fire IgE, a mast cell needs a trigger, allergen cross-linking. And the extra C in the connective-tissue type stands for chymase.

Where it breaks: other cytokines such as interleukin 21 may hold IgE switching back; mast cells mature under signals from the tissue they settle in; and hyper IgE syndromes have several genetic causes, not one.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: IL-21 may hold IgE switching back
Mast cells mature under tissue signals

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Make IgE: IL-4/IL-13 → STAT6 + CD40–CD40L → NF-κB”, “Fire IgE: cross-link → histamine, tryptase now · leukotrienes, PGD2 next · tryptase within hours”.

cues.text: A B cell switches to IgE only with an interleukin 4 or 13 signal plus the CD40 ligand handshake, and a cross-linked mast cell releases stored histamine and tryptase within minutes while also making leukotrienes and prostaglandin D2, so tryptase must be drawn within hours.

props.label: Make IgE: IL-4/IL-13 → STAT6 + CD40–CD40L → NF-κB
Fire IgE: histamine, tryptase now · leukotrienes, PGD2 next

explanation.what: Plain language: to make IgE, a B cell needs a chemical message plus a direct touch from a helper T cell; if the touch is missing, the B cell stays stuck making IgM, and in some inherited conditions IgE is made in huge excess. Once IgE sits on mast cells, an allergen that bridges two IgE molecules makes the cell dump stored chemicals immediately and then make new ones. Scientific terms: class-switch recombination, IL-4, IL-13, STAT6, CD40, CD40 ligand (CD40L), NF-κB, ε germline transcription, activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID), X-linked hyper-IgM (CD40L deficiency), hyper-IgE syndrome (HIES), STAT3, DOCK8, FcεRI, cross-linking, tryptase, chymase, carboxypeptidase, cysteinyl leukotrienes (LTC4, LTD4, LTE4), 5-lipoxygenase, prostaglandin D2, cyclooxygenase, hematopoietic PGD synthase.
explanation.why: IL-4 activates STAT6 and CD40–CD40L activates NF-κB; their binding sites lie next to each other and act together to drive ε germline transcription and AID, so losing CD40L blocks switching to IgG, IgA and IgE alike. Mast-cell granules hold preformed mediators released within minutes of FcεRI cross-linking, while lipid mediators and cytokines must be synthesized first.
explanation.measure: CD40L deficiency: normal or elevated IgM, absent or strongly reduced IgG, IgA, IgE (Durandy 2012). Hyper-IgE: IgE above 2,000 IU/mL is markedly elevated; STAT3-HIES typically 2,000–100,000 IU/mL with eosinophilia (Galletta 2024). Tryptase: peak ~1–2 h, half-life ~2 h, back to baseline within ~24 h; acute sample plus baseline at least 24 h later (Beck 2019).
explanation.differs: CD40L deficiency (switch fails, IgM only) vs STAT3-HIES (IgE excess); mucosal mast cells (tryptase only) vs connective-tissue mast cells (tryptase, chymase, carboxypeptidase); preformed mediators (histamine, proteases) vs newly made mediators (leukotrienes, PGD2, cytokines); sensitization (detectable allergen-specific IgE) vs allergy (sensitization plus clinically relevant symptoms triggered by the culprit allergen).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: pick the defect behind high IgM with low IgG/IgA/IgE, recognize Job syndrome from IgE >2,000 IU/mL with abscesses and pneumatoceles, identify the 5-lipoxygenase products that constrict airways at far lower doses than histamine, and judge a late tryptase.

mnemonic.text: To MAKE IgE a B cell needs a SIGNAL (IL-4/IL-13 → STAT6) and a HANDSHAKE (CD40–CD40L). To FIRE IgE a mast cell needs a TRIGGER (allergen cross-linking). The second C in MCTC is for Chymase and Connective tissue.
mnemonic.explanation: Links the two switching signals to CD40L deficiency and separates mast-cell subtypes by protease.
mnemonic.limitation: Other cytokines such as IL-21 may suppress IgE switching; mast cells mature under growth factors from the tissue they settle in; hyper-IgE syndromes have several genetic causes (STAT3, DOCK8 and others).

analogyLimitations: The mast-cell and T–B cell drawings are schematic, not micrographs.
IgE ranges in hyper-IgE syndrome come from one review and may fall with age.
takeaway: A B cell switches to IgE only with an interleukin 4 or 13 signal plus the CD40 ligand handshake, and a cross-linked mast cell releases stored histamine and tryptase within minutes while also making leukotrienes and prostaglandin D2, so tryptase must be drawn within hours.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy has Pneumocystis pneumonia. Serum IgM is elevated, while IgG, IgA and IgE are almost undetectable. Which defect best explains this pattern?

options.rationale: Correct. Without CD40L the B cell lacks the second switching signal, so IgM is normal or high while IgG, IgA and IgE are absent or low; it is X-linked and causes opportunistic infections.
Incorrect. STAT3 hyper-IgE syndrome shows markedly raised IgE, not absent IgE.

options.text: Loss of the FcεRI receptor on mast cells
options.rationale: Incorrect. FcεRI binds IgE on mast cells; it does not control B-cell class switching to IgG and IgA.
Incorrect. More IL-4/STAT6 signalling promotes IgE switching; it would not abolish IgG and IgA.

questions.stem: Which mast-cell mediator is newly synthesized through the 5-lipoxygenase pathway and causes bronchoconstriction at doses far lower than histamine?

options.rationale: Correct. LTD4 is a cysteinyl leukotriene made via 5-lipoxygenase and LTC4 synthase; inhaled LTC4 and LTD4 constrict airways at doses several orders of magnitude lower than histamine.
Incorrect. Histamine is preformed in granules and is less potent as a bronchoconstrictor.
Incorrect. Tryptase is a preformed granule protease, not a lipid mediator.
Incorrect. PGD2 is newly made, but through the cyclooxygenase pathway, not 5-lipoxygenase.

questions.stem: A patient had a suspected anaphylactic reaction. The only tryptase sample was collected 3 days later and is within the reference interval. How should this be interpreted?

options.text: It cannot exclude anaphylaxis; it can serve as a baseline for comparison with an acute sample
options.rationale: Correct. Tryptase peaks about 1–2 hours after onset and returns toward baseline within about 24 hours, so a day-3 value reflects baseline.
Incorrect. The sampling window had closed, and not every anaphylaxis raises tryptase.

options.text: It proves the reaction was not IgE-mediated
options.rationale: Incorrect. A late normal tryptase says nothing about the mechanism.

options.text: Histamine should be measured on the same day-3 sample instead
options.rationale: Incorrect. Histamine has an even shorter half-life than tryptase and would also have returned to baseline.

references.usedFor: CSR replaces the μ constant region with a downstream one (IgG, IgA, IgE) keeping the V region, deleting intervening DNA; CSR deficiencies show normal or elevated IgM with absent or reduced IgG, IgA, IgE; CD40L deficiency is X-linked and the most frequent CSR-D, with opportunistic infections (Pneumocystis, Cryptosporidium).

claims.text: IgE switching needs IL-4/IL-13 → STAT6 plus CD40–CD40L → NF-κB, driving ε germline transcription and AID; V region kept.
CD40L deficiency: X-linked; normal or high IgM with absent or low IgG, IgA, IgE; opportunistic infections.
Hyper-IgE >2,000 IU/mL; STAT3 (AD, Job) and DOCK8 (AR) forms; STAT3-HIES IgE 2,000–100,000 IU/mL, eosinophilia, eczema, cold staphylococcal abscesses, pneumatoceles.
Allergen cross-linking of IgE on FcεRI releases preformed mediators within minutes; lipid mediators made new; cytokines over hours.
Mucosal mast cells: tryptase only; connective-tissue mast cells: tryptase, chymase, carboxypeptidase.

Cys-LTs via 5-lipoxygenase/LTC4 synthase (LTC4 → LTD4 → LTE4); inhaled LTC4 and LTD4 bronchoconstrict at doses several orders of magnitude lower than histamine, LTE4 is weaker; PGD2 via the cyclooxygenase pathway and hematopoietic PGD synthase.
Tryptase peaks ~1–2 h, half-life ~2 h, back to baseline within ~24 h; acute plus baseline sampling; not raised in every anaphylaxis.
Allergy = sensitization plus clinically relevant symptoms (Figure 56 anchor).

Reviewer details not taught: mucosal mast cells’ high IL-5 dependence and C5a unresponsiveness; histamine 3–8 pg/cell and 10× basophil content; FcεRI receptor numbers; exact “up to 1000×” potency; reviewer’s HIES upper bound of 50,000 kU/L.
claims.note: Not verified in this session; not taught as fact.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 56 Hit 7 (and the Number Vault) gives hyper-IgE syndrome IgE as 2,000–50,000 kU/L. Galletta 2024 reports 2,000–100,000 IU/mL in STAT3-HIES, notes IgE may decrease with age, and describes several genetic forms (STAT3 autosomal dominant = Job; DOCK8 autosomal recessive; PGM3 and others) (register flag rv-hies-ige-range).

Ch. 56 Hit 15 states PGD2 comes via COX-2. Krystel-Whittemore 2015 states mast cells express COX-1 and COX-2, and Rittchen 2019 cites a study in which human lung mast-cell PGD2 relied largely on COX-1 with COX-2 absent; the lesson teaches “cyclooxygenase pathway” only (register flag rv-pgd2-cox-isoform).

Ch. 56 Hit 15 (and the Number Vault) says the cysteinyl leukotrienes LTC4/LTD4/LTE4 are up to 1000× more potent bronchoconstrictors than histamine. Kanaoka & Boyce 2014 report inhaled LTC4 and LTD4 acting at doses several log-fold lower than histamine, but describe LTE4 as a weaker bronchoconstrictor than LTC4 and LTD4; the lesson attributes the potency to LTC4 and LTD4 only (register flag rv-cyslt-lte4-potency).

morphology.note: No micrographs; the mast cell and T–B cell contact are shown as cards. The reviewer’s Figure 56 illustration is not reused.
